newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbeks to sell 1.1 bcm gas to Tajiks in '97.
newsitem.headline: Uzbeks to sell 1.1 bcm gas to Tajiks in '97.

text.p: Uzbekistan will supply Tajikistan with 1.1 billion cubic metres (bcm) of natural gas this year, according to an agreement signed by prime ministers of the two former Soviet Central Asian republics late on Monday.
"The amount is nearly the same as last year," Faizullo Nasyrov, councillor to the Tajik ambassador to Uzbekistan, told Reuters.
Nasyrov could not say what price Tajikistan would pay for the Uzbek supplies.

Russia's Interfax news agency said Tajikistan had asked the Uzbek government to reduce the price this year to $50 per 1,000 cubic metres from the current $55. World prices are around $70 per 1,000 cubic metres.
Tajikistan, devastated by four years of civil war, owes its resource-rich neighbour Uzbekistan $200 million, including $28 million for gas supplies in 1996, Nasyrov said.
But he noted that Tajikistan's gas debt had fallen from $60.2 million in January last year.
